title: Implement Bayesian trend-fission canary and weighted fallback policy
author: Priya Narayanan
description:
Context: production canaries have been noisy for slow, multi-timescale degradations where short-term variability masks a persistent upward latency trend. Existing percentile-based detectors either fire too early on bursts or too late on slow drifts. This PR introduces 'Bayesian Trend Fission' — an online decomposition that separates short-term noisy residuals from a long-term trend using a compact Bayesian state estimator, and a policy that translates fission outputs into a weighted fallback/traffic-shed decision for rollouts.

Motivation: reduce false-positives from bursty traffic while catching gradual regressions within the canary window, enabling safer staged cutovers and automatic protective fallback when needed.

What changed (high level):
- New module: pkg/perf/canary/bayesian_fission.go (implements an online two-component state-space model with conjugate updates optimized for streaming)
- Canary evaluator: canary/evaluator/fission_evaluator.go (wraps multi-signal fusion including the fission outputs, SLO-aware cost penalty, and an uncertainty-weighted decision rule)
- Fallback policy: routing/weighted_fallback.go (implements gradual traffic offload and proportional fallback to the previous model variant / cheaper quantized variant)
- Metrics and tracing: observability/canary_fission.metrics.yaml and added tracing spans to the evaluator and routing path
- Unit + integration tests: e2e/perf/canary_fission_test.go and unit tests for statistical properties
- Examples & docs: docs/ops/canary_fission.md with configuration knobs and recommended deployment recipes

Commit summary:
- 7f4a1d2: initial Bayesian fission estimator and tests
- d2ab9e7: evaluator integration + uncertainty scoring
- 1c3bb44: weighted fallback policy and routing hooks
- 8a9f0b1: metrics, dashboards, and alerts
- fc21c64: docs + CI fixes

Implementation notes:
- The estimator uses a two-state Gaussian linear dynamical model (short/noise, long/trend) with conjugate Normal-Inverse-Gamma priors for online updates. We chose closed-form updates to avoid heavy compute on the canary path; typical per-probe cost is ~60 microseconds on x86.
- The evaluator fuses the fission trend posterior mean and variance with existing latency percentile signals and throughput-weighted importance; decisions are made using a probabilistic exceedance score (Pr[trend + residual > SLO] under posterior) and an adaptive threshold calibrated to historical canary profiles.
- Weighted fallback reduces canary traffic in proportion to the exceedance score; at high confidence it will (a) divert to the previous model variant (if pinned) and (b) optionally switch to a lower-cost quantized variant. Both actions are executed via the routing layer and are reversible by the rollout controller.

Testing & benchmarks:
- Simulated traffic suite (e2e) injected gradual + bursty patterns. Results: for slow-drifts (0.5–1.5% latency/day) detection time reduced by median 22% compared to our percentile-only detector while reducing false positives on bursty traces by 45%.
- Microbenchmarks: evaluator adds ~0.6ms median overhead to canary probe cycle on our smallest canary instance; within acceptable SLO for canary windows.

Observability:
- New metrics: bayes_fission.trend_mean, bayes_fission.trend_var, bayes_fission.exceedance_prob, canary.weighted_fallback_fraction
- Dashboards: updated Canary Overview to include trend diagnostic heatmaps and uncertainty ribbons
- Alerts: added an INFO-level alert for sustained high variance in fission posterior (to catch model mismatch)

Review & CI:
- Initial CI run failed due to a flaky test in e2e/perf (race on mock time). I fixed the test harness and reran.
- Integration cluster run (staging) executed a shadow canary for 24h; results attached in the PR artifacts.
- Final CI: all unit/integration checks passed; canary e2e was green on rerun.

Review conversation summary:
- Ethan requested explanation on why conjugate updates vs lightweight particle filter; reply noted CPU predictability and simpler memory profile for online path.
- Marta requested a guard to avoid oscillation when trend variance spikes; added hysteresis and a min-smoothed-fallback-rate to the routing logic.
- Jonah ran the staging canary and asked for tighter default thresholds for enterprise tenants; added tenant-level overrides and documented them.

Safety & rollout:
- Feature gated behind 'bayesian_fission' feature flag and disabled by default for hosted customers; enabled by default for dedicated/test clusters.
- Config knobs: window_size, short_term_decay, trend_process_noise, exceedance_threshold, fallback_max_fraction.
- Migration: none required; config is additive.

Rollout/testing plan:
- Canary in staging (shadow) for 48h — completed during this PR.
- Gradual opt-in to non-critical production traffic, first to internal services, then to a small subset of customer traffic (<=5%).
- Monitor bayes_fission.exceedance_prob, canary.false_positive_rate, and routing.fallback_fraction.

Related work: references two tickets ENG-2124 (drift detection), ENG-2199 (canary routing hooks).

Files changed (high-level):
- pkg/perf/canary/bayesian_fission.go
- canary/evaluator/fission_evaluator.go
- routing/weighted_fallback.go
- observability/canary_fission.metrics.yaml
- e2e/perf/canary_fission_test.go
- docs/ops/canary_fission.md
- pkg/perf/canary/bayesian_fission_test.go
- dashboards/canary_overview.json
- internal/utils/stat_helpers.go
- ci/scripts/run_canary_e2e.sh

Troubleshooting notes:
- If you see elevated bayes_fission.trend_var in staging, check the probe timestamp alignment (we require monotonic timestamps) and verify traffic shape is within expected bounds.
- To tune sensitivity, adjust trend_process_noise up to allow larger trend updates without triggering fallback.

Merge outcome: merged via squash after two approvals and CI green.

Release notes: "Introduce Bayesian Trend-Fission canary evaluator and uncertainty-weighted fallback policy; reduces false positives on bursty traffic and improves detection of gradual regressions. Feature is feature-flagged and disabled by default for hosted customers."

release_notes: Introduce Bayesian Trend-Fission canary evaluator and uncertainty-weighted fallback policy. Improves detection latency for gradual regressions and reduces false positives on bursty traffic. Feature-flagged; tenant override knobs added.
notes_for_oncall: If canary reports frequent fallback_fraction > 0.3 for internal non-critical canaries, temporarily disable bayesian_fission feature flag and escalate to perf team. Watch bayes_fission.trend_var and canary.false_positive_rate metrics.
